I farm by what I saw work here, not by big talk. This year I will still keep wheat-maize as my main way, because that is what feeds the house and brings steady money. On my 9 mu, I will keep 6 mu in wheat-maize, then I will leave 2 mu for cotton and 1 mu for mungbean. That way I do not put all my money in one crop. Wheat and maize are the backbone, cotton gives cash if the price is decent, and mungbean does not need as much fertilizer, so it helps me save a little on input cost. I do not like cutting fertilizer too hard. If I save a little and the crop goes thin, I lose much more at harvest. So I will follow what has worked in recent years around me: enough base fertilizer, then topdress when the crop is really growing. I have well water, so I will not let wheat dry at jointing and filling, and I will give maize water around the big growth time. Cotton needs more watching for insects, so I will spray that more times. Mungbean I will keep simple, because it is a small piece and I do not want to pour too much money into it.
